plantagenet-0.name: Henry II
plantagenet-0.era: c.1170, Angevin England and western France
plantagenet-0.attire: Long wool tunic, patterned silk mantle, narrow belt and low open crown.
plantagenet-0.props: Rolled writ and plain sword hilt.
plantagenet-0.setting: Romanesque hall at Chinon, limestone arch.
plantagenet-0.likeness: Fontevraud effigy supplies royal costume context; mature compact face and reddish beard are interpretive, not a proven portrait.
plantagenet-0.avoid: No full plate armour or Renaissance ruff.

plantagenet-1.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
plantagenet-1.attire: Long fitted gown, pale veil under crown, rich mantle.
plantagenet-1.props: Open illuminated book, held below chest.
plantagenet-1.setting: Romanesque abbey arcade with warm Aquitaine light.
plantagenet-1.likeness: Reading pose derives from her Fontevraud effigy; facial individuality is reconstructed rather than claimed as a life likeness.
plantagenet-1.avoid: No exposed fantasy corset, hennin or Tudor hood.

plantagenet-2.name: Richard I
plantagenet-2.attire: Mail hauberk and coif lowered around neck, simple surcoat and mantle.
plantagenet-2.props: Straight sword and shield at lower side.
plantagenet-2.setting: Stone coastal fortress with distant Mediterranean light, an interpretive crusading setting.
plantagenet-2.likeness: Fontevraud effigy is commemorative evidence, not an exact life portrait; use a mature bearded face.
plantagenet-2.avoid: No late-medieval plate harness, horned helmet or modern national flag.

plantagenet-3.name: John
plantagenet-3.attire: Rich long tunic, mantle, small open crown.
plantagenet-3.props: Great seal beside a rolled charter.
plantagenet-3.likeness: Worcester preserves an early royal effigy; use its crowned, bearded convention without asserting portrait accuracy.
plantagenet-3.avoid: Show a sealed charter, not John signing Magna Carta with a modern pen.

plantagenet-4.name: Henry III
plantagenet-4.attire: Long ceremonial robe with narrow trim, mantle, open crown.
plantagenet-4.setting: Westminster Gothic building works suggested through an arch.
plantagenet-4.likeness: Abbey burial and rebuilding are documented; live facial modelling is interpretive, informed by his effigy.
plantagenet-4.avoid: No Tudor rose, full plate armour or completed modern Abbey skyline.

plantagenet-5.name: Edward I
plantagenet-5.attire: Mail with modest reinforcing plates, crimson mantle; tall restrained silhouette.
plantagenet-5.likeness: Abbey account records red-and-gold royal burial dress and crimson mantle; living face is reconstructed.
plantagenet-5.avoid: No Gothic full plate harness or literal war hammer from later epithet.

plantagenet-6.name: Edward II
plantagenet-6.attire: Long silk robe, mantle and open leaf crown.
plantagenet-6.likeness: Gloucester alabaster effigy provides commemorative reference; soft individual facial features are interpretive.
plantagenet-6.avoid: No feminizing caricature or execution imagery.

plantagenet-7.name: Edward III
plantagenet-7.attire: Mid-fourteenth-century transitional armour with mail at joints; restrained royal mantle.
plantagenet-7.likeness: Abbey bronze shows long hair and beard; adapt mature features rather than copy the late-life death-mask expression.
plantagenet-7.avoid: No sixteenth-century armour; no three-lily French quartering for this date.

plantagenet-8.name: Philippa of Hainault
plantagenet-8.attire: Reticulated headdress, fitted laced bodice, buttoned sleeves and loose mantle.
plantagenet-8.props: One hand on cloak cord; small closed book.
plantagenet-8.setting: Windsor chamber with Flemish woven hanging.
plantagenet-8.likeness: Her Westminster alabaster effigy supplies a full face and substantial figure; mature warmth is an artistic interpretation.
plantagenet-8.avoid: No slim generic maiden, Tudor hood or horned hennin.

plantagenet-9.name: Richard II
plantagenet-9.attire: Rich patterned robe, fine open crown, white-hart jewel.
plantagenet-9.likeness: Wilton Diptych provides contemporary idealized royal image and white-hart symbolism; preserve slender youthful countenance without treating it as photography.
plantagenet-9.avoid: No battle armour, sinister caricature or later Tudor ornament.

plantagenet-10.name: Edward the Black Prince
plantagenet-10.attire: Fourteenth-century plate elements over mail, short heraldic jupon.
plantagenet-10.props: Bascinet under arm, sword low; feather motif secondary.
plantagenet-10.likeness: Canterbury funerary armour and Westminster statuette anchor material culture; living facial expression is reconstructed.
plantagenet-10.avoid: Do not present black armour as established origin of his later nickname; no sixteenth-century harness.

plantagenet-11.name: Joan of Kent
plantagenet-11.attire: Silk fitted gown, fine veil and modest jeweled fillet.
plantagenet-11.props: Silver cup held below portrait center.
plantagenet-11.likeness: IHR records her marriage, Aquitaine household and silver vessels; face, exact dress and room are explicitly plausible reconstruction.
plantagenet-11.avoid: She was Princess of Wales, not a crowned queen; no invented exact likeness or sexualized scandal imagery.

plantagenet-12.name: Geoffrey of Anjou
plantagenet-12.era: c.1140, Anjou and Maine; Geoffrey V, Henry II's father
plantagenet-12.attire: Twelfth-century long tunic and mantle; modest cap.
plantagenet-12.props: Blue shield with gold lion motifs and sword, adapted from enamel; small broom sprig symbolic.
plantagenet-12.likeness: Le Mans museum's funerary enamel is the reference, a stylized posthumous image; facial realism and broom placement are interpretation.
plantagenet-12.avoid: Do not confuse Geoffrey V with his son Geoffrey of Nantes; no English royal crown or plate armour.

plantagenet-13.name: Isabella of France
plantagenet-13.attire: Silk gown and fine linen veil, narrow crown; restrained white-and-blue palette.
plantagenet-13.likeness: English Heritage documents Eltham patronage and white velvet worn in 1316; adult face and diplomatic scene are reconstruction.
plantagenet-13.avoid: No wolf pelt or villain stereotype; epithet is later hostile rhetoric.

tudor-0.name: Henry VII
tudor-0.attire: Dark velvet cap, fur-lined gown, patterned doublet, restrained gold chain.
tudor-0.likeness: NPG portrait tradition supplies narrow mature face and reserved mouth; chamber and gesture are interpretive.
tudor-0.avoid: No Henry VIII physique, Elizabethan ruff or excessive martial armour.

tudor-1.name: Elizabeth I
tudor-1.attire: Jeweled gown, lace ruff, pearls and dressed red hair.
tudor-1.setting: Dark Tudor palace chamber with modest globe at edge.
tudor-1.likeness: Darnley portrait tradition supplies recognizable long face; generated skin and expression remain interpretation.
tudor-1.avoid: Avoid confusing late Elizabethan clothing with early Tudor gable hoods.

tudor-2.name: Henry VIII
tudor-2.attire: Broad fur-trimmed gown, slashed doublet, jeweled flat bonnet, gold chain.
tudor-2.setting: Hampton Court-style brick and oak interior.
tudor-2.likeness: Holbein royal portrait tradition anchors broad stance, rounded face and short reddish beard; setting is reconstructed.
tudor-2.avoid: No medieval mail, oversized fantasy crown or execution props.

tudor-3.name: Mary I
tudor-3.attire: Pearl-edged headdress, patterned gown and purple overgown.
tudor-3.setting: Red upholstered royal chair against subdued palace wall.
tudor-3.likeness: Anthonis Mor's 1554 portrait is direct lifetime evidence; retain mature narrow face and firm mouth.
tudor-3.avoid: Do not confuse with her aunt Mary Tudor of France; no flames or caricature.

tudor-4.name: Edward VI
tudor-4.attire: High-collared embroidered doublet, short cloak, jeweled cap.
tudor-4.likeness: Royal Collection portrait tradition supplies youthful facial proportions; use a boy of about thirteen, not an adult lawgiver.
tudor-4.avoid: No beard, oversized muscles or later Elizabethan wheel ruff.

tudor-5.name: Elizabeth of York
tudor-5.attire: Early Tudor gable hood, rich square-neck gown, jeweled edging.
tudor-5.setting: Quiet royal chamber with restrained union-rose embroidery.
tudor-5.likeness: NPG portrait tradition informs pale oval face; reconstruction must acknowledge later copies rather than claim direct observation.
tudor-5.avoid: No Elizabeth I ruff or elaborate late-century hair.

tudor-6.name: Margaret Beaufort
tudor-6.attire: Black vowess gown, white linen wimple and dark hood.
tudor-6.likeness: Wewyck portrait c.1510 and NPG interpretation anchor vowess dress; elderly facial details are interpreted from posthumous evidence.
tudor-6.avoid: Not a nun, witch or seductive intriguer; avoid invented sinister props.

tudor-7.name: Edmund Tudor
tudor-7.era: c.1455, England and southwest Wales; Earl of Richmond
tudor-7.attire: Mid-fifteenth-century doublet and fur-edged gown, soft cap.
tudor-7.likeness: National Library of Wales biography identifies Henry VII's young father, not the later infant namesake; no secure living likeness used, face reconstructed at about twenty-five.
tudor-7.avoid: No royal crown, Tudor union rose or sixteenth-century ruff.

tudor-8.name: Jasper Tudor
tudor-8.era: c.1485, Welsh and Breton exile networks
tudor-8.attire: Late-fifteenth-century harness, mail collar, travel mantle.
tudor-8.setting: Pembrokeshire coastline and castle in soft focus.
tudor-8.likeness: Welsh Biography establishes campaigns, exile and mentorship; rugged mature face is explicitly invented, not a verified portrait.
tudor-8.avoid: No English royal crown or modern Welsh flag design.

tudor-9.name: Margaret Tudor
tudor-9.attire: Early-sixteenth-century royal gown, jeweled hood, rich mantle.
tudor-9.setting: Scottish palace stone chamber, restrained thistle detail.
tudor-9.likeness: Royal Collection Mytens-derived image is later evidence, not a contemporary likeness; facial specificity is cautious reconstruction.
tudor-9.avoid: Do not use NPG 1173, now identified as an unknown woman; no tartan clan costume.

tudor-10.name: Mary Tudor of France
tudor-10.attire: Early French court silk gown, jeweled hood, delicate gold necklace.
tudor-10.props: Marriage letter and a single flower.
tudor-10.setting: Loire court interior with small fleur-de-lis textile.
tudor-10.likeness: RCT documents her French marriage negotiations; exact facial likeness not established here and is interpretive. Keep visually distinct from Mary I.
tudor-10.avoid: No Mary I identification, later Elizabethan ruff or unqualified use of disputed Sittow portrait.

tudor-11.name: Arthur Tudor
tudor-11.era: c.1500, England; adolescent Prince of Wales
tudor-11.attire: Embroidered early Tudor doublet and modest dark cap.
tudor-11.likeness: NPG exhibition records Wewyck portrait made during marriage negotiations and its flower; depict a slight teenage boy.
tudor-11.avoid: Never an adult warrior or crowned king; no late-sixteenth-century costume.

tudor-12.name: Owen Tudor
tudor-12.era: c.1430–1440, Welsh courtier in English royal household
tudor-12.attire: Modest wool gown over fitted doublet, soft chaperon.
tudor-12.likeness: National Library of Wales establishes courtier identity and notes obscure early life; face, exact dress and pose are reconstructed.
tudor-12.avoid: No Tudor royal crown, union rose, caricatured Celtic warrior or secret-dagger stereotype.

tudor-13.name: Catherine of Aragon
tudor-13.era: c.1525, English queen of Castilian-Aragonese origins
tudor-13.attire: Jeweled gable hood, rich gown with square neckline and fine linen.
tudor-13.props: Small prayer book with pomegranate decoration.
tudor-13.likeness: Prefer NPG c.1520 panel and Horenbout miniature tradition; distinguish them from NPG 163, an eighteenth-century copy. Face is interpreted from accepted portrait types.
tudor-13.avoid: No exoticized Spanish costume, flamenco mantilla or confusion with Mary Tudor of France.
